The test image shows a soybean petiole/stem junction with dark brown to nearly black discoloration on the petiole, while leaves remain mostly green with some small spots. Key features: dark reddish-brown petiole discoloration, hairy stem texture visible.

Top candidates: **Anthracnose** (dark brown lesions on petioles), **Cercospora** (reddish-purple lesions on petioles), **Diaporthe** (pycnidia on stems).

**Analysis:**

**Test image features:**
- Very dark brown to nearly black uniform discoloration along the entire petiole
- Green leaves with a few small brown spots
- Hairy stem texture (normal soybean morphology)
- The main symptom is clearly on the petiole/stem junction

**Comparing candidates:**
- **Anthracnose**: "brown cankers can appear on petioles causing defoliation" — the dark brown/black petiole matches well
- **Cercospora**: "reddish-purple lesions on petioles" — possible, but test image looks more dark brown than reddish-purple
- **Diaporthe**: reference shows light tan/brown stem lesions with linear pycnidia — doesn't match the uniformly dark petiole

The test image shows the characteristic dark brown/almost black canker on the petiole that is strongly associated with Anthracnose. The Anthracnose reference shows dark lesions/acervuli on pods. The symptom description explicitly mentions "brown cankers on petioles causing defoliation" and dark acervuli. The near-black uniform darkening of the entire petiole with green leaves still present is the key signature.
